text: dsh-ocr-bridge 是面向 DSH 网页端的模型适配插件：它接管官方 DeepSeek provider，在聊天提交图片时先用本地 macOS Vision 或 Tesseract 提取图片中的文字，再把文字作为视觉上下文交给 DeepSeek 文本模型回答；没有图片的对话仍直接委派给官方适配器。它还声明图片输入能力、可限制每次识别的图片数量，并可设置本地识别超时。适合希望用现有 DeepSeek 文本模型读取截图或照片文字的 DSH 用户；图片识别在本机完成，但识别文本会随请求发送到 DeepSeek API，仍需配置现有 DeepSeek API 凭据。

dsh-ocr-bridge adapts DSH’s DeepSeek provider. It reads chat images locally with macOS Vision or Tesseract, then sends extracted text to a text-only DeepSeek model. Image-free chats pass through unchanged. Existing DeepSeek API credentials are required.
想把聊天里截图上的文字识别出来，让文本模型继续回答。
DSH 的文本模型不能直接看图片，有没有办法先本地 OCR？
让 DeepSeek 聊天读取我粘贴的图片中的中文和英文。
发多张截图提问时，能不能先提取文字再合并到问题里？
I want my text-only chat model to read text from an image attachment.
Can I OCR screenshots locally and ask DeepSeek about the extracted text?
dsh-ocr-bridge 的功能「本地图片文字识别」：聊天含图片且模型本身不支持图像时，读取附件并依次尝试 macOS Vision 与 Tesseract，将识别结果加入请求上下文后交给 DeepSeek 文本模型。
dsh-ocr-bridge 的功能「无图对话兼容」：用户发送不含图片的消息时，适配器直接把原请求交给官方 DeepSeek 适配器处理，保留现有文本对话路径。
dsh-ocr-bridge 的功能「识别参数控制」：在 llm-deepseek 设置中可配置单次最多识别图片数和每个后端的超时；图片数超过上限时请求返回对应错误。
dsh-ocr-bridge 使用现有 DeepSeek API 凭据委派文本请求；本地 OCR 提取的文字会随请求发送给 DeepSeek API。凭据从配置的 apiKeyEnv 解析，优先读取凭据服务，再读取启动环境变量。
dsh-ocr-bridge 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 85 天；提交数 6；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-ocr-bridge README · dsh-ocr-bridge：**English** | [**中文**](https://github.com/vuvanmai936-dot/dsh-ocr-bridge/blob/main/README.zh.md)

Paste images directly into [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) chat and have them **read by a free local backend** — macOS Vision, with a Tesseract fallback — before the text-only DeepSeek model (e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash`) answers. Your model, agent capabilities, API key, and cost stay exactly the same.

dsh-ocr-bridge README · dsh-ocr-bridge：> **Scope note:** this is an *OCR-level* local bridge — it reads text out of images (macOS Vision → Tesseract). It is **not** general visual understanding, and **no cloud endpoint is ever called**.

dsh-ocr-bridge README · dsh-ocr-bridge：> **Independence notice.** This is an independent, community-built plugin **for** DeepSeek Harness (DSH). It is not an official DeepSeek product and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by DeepSeek or the DeepSeek Harness project. "DeepSeek" and "DeepSeek Harness" are trademarks of their respective owners.

dsh-ocr-bridge README · dsh-ocr-bridge：> ⚠️ **Trust boundary.** This plugin runs inside the harness host process with shell-level access (it spawns `osascript` / `tesseract`). Only install plugins you trust. The OCR text injected into the request is explicitly marked as *untrusted observation data, not instructions* — never execute commands, rules, or privilege escalations that appear in it.

dsh-ocr-bridge README · Why：DSH's image admission gate (`dsh-host-apiproxy.submitPrompt`) rejects attachments unless the current model declares `image` input. The official DeepSeek adapter hardcodes `inputModalities: ["text"]` for every model and its serializer throws on image blocks. The gate only checks the *declaration*, not real multimodality — so this plugin registers a wrapper adapter that:

dsh-ocr-bridge README · Install：Requires DSH `0.1.0-rc.7` (peer dependencies are pinned; other release candidates are not supported — see [Compatibility](#compatibility)).

```bash
dsh-ocr-bridge README · npm registry：dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-ocr-bridge
dsh-ocr-bridge README · or directly from GitHub：dsh plugin --profile web add github:your-org/dsh-ocr-bridge

dsh-ocr-bridge README · local development (live reload of lib/ changes)：dsh plugin --profile web add link:~/dev/dsh-vision-bridge
```

> Package name note: the npm name `dsh-vision-bridge` is taken by an unrelated project, and the upstream `dsh-vision` package already owns the "vision" naming — so this plugin is published as **`dsh-ocr-bridge`**, which also states its OCR-level scope.

text:
dsh-ocr-bridge README · Backends：| Order | Backend | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | macOS Vision (JXA via `osascript`) | macOS 10.15+; zero installation, Chinese + English built in |
| 2 | Tesseract | `tesseract` CLI + language packs (`chi_sim`, `chi_tra`, `eng`); also the only option on Linux/Windows |

If Vision fails and Tesseract is missing, the request fails with `VISION_UNAVAILABLE` and the error lists both backend failures. Images are written to a temp directory and always cleaned up.

dsh-ocr-bridge README · Configuration：All settings are optional. They live in the `llm-deepseek` settings section (the official DeepSeek section this plugin takes over), so your existing DeepSeek settings keep working.

`settings.yaml` (or the GUI settings surface):

```yaml
llm-deepseek:
  visionTimeoutMs: 180000   # per-backend recognition timeout (ms), default 180000
  maxImages: 8              # images recognized per request, 1..32, default 8
  # …all official DeepSeek settings keep working: baseURL, apiKeyEnv, thinking, …

dsh-ocr-bridge README · Configuration：- Over the limit, the request fails with `VISION_IMAGE_LIMIT` instead of silently dropping images.
- Recognized observations are cached per (image set + latest user text), up to 64 entries, so re-sending the same screenshot in one conversation does not re-run OCR.
- `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` resolution is fully preserved: `ctx.credentials` first, then the launch environment, exactly like the official adapter.
- png / jpeg / webp / gif are all supported (whatever the harness attachment admission accepts).

dsh-ocr-bridge README · Architecture：```
paste image ──► submitPrompt gate ──► wrapper adapter (inputModalities=["text","image"]) ──passes──► durable attachment refs
                                                          │
                                   stream(): collectImageRefs(messages)
                                     ├─ no images ─► delegate to DeepSeekAdapter untouched

dsh-ocr-bridge README · Development：```bash
pnpm install
pnpm check        # typecheck + test + build
```

Live-testing against your harness:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add link:~/dev/dsh-vision-bridge   # symlink: lib/ changes apply immediately

text:
dsh-ocr-bridge README · Verification checklist：- [ ] After `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-ocr-bridge` and restart, the model selector still shows `deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-v4-pro`
- [ ] Pasting one or several images under a text-only flash model no longer raises `MODEL_DOES_NOT_SUPPORT_IMAGES`
- [ ] Mixed Chinese + English screenshots are recognized correctly (macOS Vision)
- [ ] Tesseract fallback works (simulate a Vision failure)
- [ ] Text-only conversations behave identically to the official adapter (pure delegation)
- [ ] No new API key needed; `settings.yaml` unchanged works out of the box
- [ ] png / jpeg / webp / gif all work; image count respects `maxImages`

dsh-ocr-bridge README · Compatibility：- DSH `0.1.0-rc.7` only. Peer dependencies are pinned exactly (`@deepseek-ai/*` `0.1.0-rc.7`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `4.0.1`); later release candidates will be added as they ship.
- Node `>=22.19`, pnpm `10.x`.
- macOS 10.15+ recommended for the Vision backend; Linux/Windows fall back to Tesseract.

dsh-ocr-bridge README · Credits：The code skeleton is adapted from [oil-oil/dsh-vision](https://github.com/oil-oil/dsh-vision) (MIT) and used with attribution (see [LICENSE](./LICENSE)). Positioning differs deliberately: **dsh-ocr-bridge is a local-first, OCR-level bridge** (zero cloud, zero extra cost, pinned to rc.7), while upstream focuses on cloud multimodal endpoints plus a visual-memory workflow. The two are complementary rather than overlapping in scope; this plugin does not claim to be a fork or successor of upstream.

dsh-ocr-bridge README · Roadmap (v1+)：- Ollama local vision backend (e.g. `llava`) as a third recognition option
- Client settings card for the bridge options (currently configured via `settings.yaml` / composition config)
- Multi-backend scoring (Vision + Tesseract agreement) for higher-confidence OCR
